A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Module-Switching Defense (MSD) work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching content across substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original two-layer-network simulations and backdoor-defense experiments on SST-2, MNLI, AG News and CIFAR-10, including appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds original TinyImageNet, CNN, collusion, adaptive-attack and mechanism-analysis results.

M1.justification: The five-rule evolutionary switching framework remains. However, Algorithm 2 changes suspect-class identification from majority voting over model-specific choices to summing classwise cosine-distance scores. v2 also adapts switching to convolution–batch-normalization modules and uses pooled convolutional features for CNN candidate selection.

E1.justification: v2 adds TinyImageNet's 200-class image-classification coverage while retaining the original datasets. It also evaluates distinct threat scenarios absent from v1: colluding models sharing backdoors, attackers adapting to a known switching strategy, Adaptive-Patch attacks, inconsistent target labels and identical triggers with different targets.

E2.justification: WAG becomes an evaluated comparator in the two-layer simulations in Section 3 and Appendix G; v1's corresponding simulations compared pretrained, fine-tuned and switched networks without WAG. The existing deep-model defense comparators—WAG, TIES, DARE, Z-Def, ONION, CutMix and ShrinkPad—remain.

E3.justification: Original benchmark splits, training schedules, CACC/ASR metrics and clean-data budgets are retained. Added experiments introduce four-model fusion, ResNet-18/50 configurations, adaptive retraining with unselected modules frozen, and simulations varying backdoor perturbation strength. New utility-loss and computational-efficiency measurements also expand the evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The existing heuristic-rule, clean-data-budget and poisoning-rate studies remain. v2 adds second-order-interaction diagnostics, individual utility-loss analysis, overlap analysis across searched strategies, efficiency comparisons, and robustness tests for collusion, adaptation and label/trigger mismatches. These substantially expand the questions investigated beyond ordinary benchmark performance.

E5.justification: Both versions report defense results averaged over three seeds. v2 adds explicit mean±standard-deviation reporting for second-order ratios: across runs in Table 4 and across 24 layers in Table 5. Appendix F adds utility-loss distribution and tail summaries. Increased runs for retained defense experiments are not established.

E6.justification: Original benchmark and ablation values are largely retained, but substantial new results appear. For example, v2 Table 13 reports 20.5% MSD versus 31.9% WAG average ASR for collusive BadNet/InsertSent fusion. Table 11 reports TinyImageNet BadNet+WaNet ASR of 0.4% versus 8.6%, with CACC of 84.2% versus 88.2%. CNN, adaptive-attack and mechanism results further expand the evidence.

T1.justification: v1 provides simulation objectives and a weight-update decomposition without formal guarantees. v2 adds Definitions 1–4, a divergence bound against WAG, an existence proposition and proofs in Appendix D. Appendices E–F introduce a utility-loss identity and related definitions. The analysis assumes shared pretrained weights, identity activation and omission of second-order interactions.

C1.justification: v2 adds theoretical advantage over WAG and robustness to collusive backdoors as central abstract/introduction claims, and explicitly extends claimed applicability to CNNs. v1 primarily presents empirical module switching for Transformer models. Defense using few potentially compromised models was already claimed in v1 and is retained.

C2.justification: v2 explains collusion as reducing WAG to fewer-model behavior and interprets low strategy overlap as evidence of broadly distributed disruption. Appendix A newly limits demonstrated applicability to classification. Conversely, Section 5.2 replaces v1's explicit three-model exception with consistent-superiority wording, although Table 12 retains MSD's 13.0% versus WAG's 11.5% ASR in that case.

D1.justification: v2 provides a code-repository address and reproducibility statement, whereas v1 promises future switching-template release. It identifies the search CPU, reports 2.6/4.3-hour two-/four-model searches, and supplies selection/merging timings and dataset-license information. These refine disclosure; the earlier generic six-hour estimate does not establish a comparable runtime speedup.

R1.justification: v2 substantially broadens positioning through mixture-of-experts and one-shot federated-learning motivation, explicit discussion of WAG/DAM model-resource demands, and separation of detection from model repair. Related work adds substantial trigger-inversion, purification and unlearning coverage, including UNICORN, BaDExpert and UNIT. These citations are not additional evaluated defense baselines.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and substantial method exposition are rewritten. Section 3 is reorganized into setup, theoretical analysis and empirical analysis; heuristic details move to the appendix, and the appendix structure is extensively reorganized. The shortened title and new reproducibility, limitations and disclosure sections accompany these narrative changes.

P2.justification: The two-column layout becomes a single-column conference format, and main tables are reorganized into paired blocks. Shallow-network bar charts become scatterplots; new distribution, overlap and CNN/four-model strategy figures appear. The original three-model Table 3 moves to appendix Table 12, alongside substantial new result tables.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence about generality and deployment robustness through CNN, TinyImageNet, collusive, adaptive and target-mismatch evaluations, addressing important gaps in v1's deep-model testing. Mechanism diagnostics and code-access information also improve assessability and reproducibility. Material caveats remain: Section 4.4 extrapolates the approximate two-layer divergence bound into an unsupported deep-model defense guarantee, some new results incur accuracy costs, and the three-model superiority prose overlooks the retained Table 12 exception.
